kennedy-survives-wins-nomination.summary: In this world, the voters I interviewed lean 0.9 points further toward Nixon than the same people did in 1968 as it was. Arkansas, Connecticut, Georgia, New York and 1 more flip, but Nixon still wins, 393–117–28. The closest call is Missouri, which holds for Nixon by 1.1 points. Humphrey wins in 28 of 100 draws. Extremely low confidence. Historical evidence is thin: loose analogies or weak sources only.
assumptions: The Democratic nominee is replaced by a different man with a distinct profile: stronger with Black, Catholic and poor voters and with anti-war Democrats, weaker with some Southern and conservative whites. The ballot line for that nominee is rewritten with his news, and the backbone's observed 1968 shifts are adjusted accordingly.
howIGotThis: What changed: Robert Kennedy is not killed in June, and he is the nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1961.

What historians found (11 findings, weak evidence): No direct evidence exists on a Kennedy general election, since he was killed in June 1968. Spring polls had Kennedy roughly level with or slightly behind Nixon, and he did well among Black voters, Catholics and working-class whites in primaries. Sources suggest he might have cut Wallace's union vote, but Wallace likely held most Southern whites.
The numbers: the 1960 and 1970 census counts interpolated to 1968 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1968 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

facts: On 31 October the President announced that all bombing of North Vietnam would stop the next day, following progress in the Paris talks.
Representatives of the Saigon government and the National Liberation Front have been invited to take part in broadened negotiations.
Officials say the pause rests on an understanding that the talks will proceed promptly and that North Vietnam will respect the demilitarized zone.

before.reason: Harry Ellis is a 68-year-old white rural Indiana man employed in industrial work, living through turbulent times.
